I am 60 this year, and I have farmed Quzhou land for 40 years. I do not chase the highest possible yield on paper. On 15 mu with only 2 people in the household, I have to keep the work manageable and the cash use steady. So I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is still the safest income here, and I will leave a smaller piece in cotton. I have enough experience to adjust rates a little by crop and field condition, but I still lean on what has worked locally. Wheat and maize are my base; cotton is for extra cash, but I will not put too much area into it because picking takes labor and at my age that matters.

For this year, I will put 10 mu into winter wheat followed immediately by summer maize, and 5 mu into cotton. On wheat, I want a stable stand and steady grain filling, so I will use improved seed, put most phosphorus and potassium into the base fertilizer, and split nitrogen between sowing and jointing. I have well water, so I will irrigate at the key times instead of gambling on rainfall alone, but I will not overwater because pumping costs money. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I will use simple field prep and sow quickly after wheat harvest. I will fertilize a bit heavier at planting and then topdress once around the big-bell stage. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller, use decent seed, and manage fertilizer in more splits because cotton responds better that way. Cotton can bring cash, but it also asks for more hands and more attention to insects, so I keep it at a size I can still manage.
